The Prime Ministers of the Solomon Islands 🇸🇧 and PNG 🇵🇬 Ready to Facilitate Dialogue between West Papua and Indonesia. Solomon Islands PM: The Papua Issue Must Be Discussed Openly During a bilateral meeting in Port Moresby, Papua New Guinea, Solomon Islands Prime Minister Matthew Wale and Papua New Guinea Prime Minister James Marape directly addressed the situation in West Papua from the perspectives of humanitarian concerns and the bonds shared by Melanesian nations. Key points raised during the meeting included: 1. Strengthening the Melanesian Spearhead Group (MSG) Matthew Wale emphasized that the MSG must remain an independent sub-regional organization, free from the influence of external interests. He noted that the MSG plays a vital role in fostering unity and cooperation among Melanesian nations. 2. Discussing the Situation in West Papua The two leaders discussed the issue of West Papua, including the growing aspirations for independence in the region. Wale stressed the need to view this issue through a humanitarian lens while maintaining good diplomatic relations with Indonesia and avoiding a confrontational stance. 3. Encouraging Open Dialogue Matthew Wale stated that the situation in West Papua should not be a topic to be avoided. He argued that open dialogue regarding humanitarian conditions and human rights is necessary to prevent misunderstandings, suspicion, and tension among Melanesian nations. The core message of the meeting was that the West Papua issue needs to be discussed openly at the regional level, particularly from a humanitarian perspective. Matthew Wale believes that open dialogue can actually strengthen trust, reduce tension, and pave the way for a peaceful resolution. For many Melanesians, discussions regarding West Papua are viewed not merely as a political matter, but also as an expression of concern for fellow Melanesians and a reflection of humanitarian values. #Freedom #WestPapua #reelsWestPapua #realestate #reelsfb #malanesiapasific
